questions.def: Use 'a pair of' to refer to two items that are used together.
questions.question: I need to buy ___ new shoes.

questions.def: Use 'any' in questions to ask about the existence of something.
questions.question: Do you have ___ milk?

questions.def: No determiner needed as the books are specified.
questions.question: The books on the table are mine.

questions.def: Use 'much' with uncountable nouns like 'time' in negative sentences.
questions.question: I don't have ___ time to finish this.

questions.def: 'A lot of' is used before plural countable nouns.
questions.question: There are ___ people at the party.

questions.def: 'A lot of' can be used with uncountable nouns like 'money'.
questions.question: He spent ___ money on that car.

questions.def: 'Little' means almost no milk, which suits the context.
questions.question: There is ___ milk left in the fridge.

questions.def: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences when offering or asking for things.
questions.question: I need ___ information about the course.

questions.def: 'Some' is used to indicate an unspecified quantity.
questions.question: ___ students are late today.

questions.def: 'Few' means almost none, so 'a few' is more appropriate here.
questions.question: I have few friends, so I am often lonely.

questions.def: 'Every' refers to all days without exception.
questions.question: I go to the gym ___ day.

questions.def: 'All' is used to refer to the whole of a group.
questions.question: ___ cats are cute.

questions.def: 'Every' is used to refer to all members of a group, considered individually.
questions.question: ___ child needs love and attention.

questions.def: No determiner needed because context makes it specific.
questions.question: The people I met were very kindly.

questions.def: 'Other' is used to mean an alternative option.
questions.question: I have no ___ option.

questions.def: Use 'some' when requesting something.
questions.question: Can I have ___ water, please?

questions.def: Use 'any' in negative sentences.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money.

questions.def: 'Many' is used with countable nouns in questions.
questions.question: How ___ books did you read?

questions.def: Use 'the' with superlative adjectives.
questions.question: He is ___ most intelligent student in the class.

questions.def: Use 'an' before vowel sounds.
questions.question: This is ___ interesting book.

questions.def: No determiner needed before 'new car' (generic).
questions.question: I want the new car, but I can't afford it.

questions.def: 'A few' means some friends, which is positive.
questions.question: I have ___ friends who live nearby.

questions.def: 'Most' means the majority of the juice.
questions.question: She drank ___ of the juice.

questions.def: 'Most' is the correct determiner to use here.
questions.question: ___ people enjoy listening to music.

questions.def: Use 'an' before vowel sounds (engineer).
questions.question: He is a engineer at the factory.

questions.def: 'This' is used for singular things that are near.
questions.question: ___ is my favorite movie.

questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a specific dog.
questions.question: ___ dog is very friendly.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: I ate ___ apple this morning.

questions.def: Use 'some' for an unspecified quantity in positive sentences.
questions.question: I need to buy ___ milk from the store.

questions.def: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like money.
questions.question: How ___ money do you have?
